question: When self-hosting Horizon or Stellar RPC, how do HISTORY_RETENTION_COUNT and HISTORY_RETENTION_WINDOW affect database size, and why doesn't increasing the window backfill older history?

golden.answer: Retention only bounds how much history a node keeps; it never fetches older data. As of 2026-11-14 (stellar-rpc v30.0.1) RPC's HISTORY_RETENTION_WINDOW defaults to 120960 ledgers, about 7 days, and RPC backfills only with BACKFILL=true from a datastore. Horizon's HISTORY_RETENTION_COUNT defaults to 0, meaning keep everything; 518400 is the recommended 30-day setting. Missing Horizon history needs `db reingest range`.
keyFacts: A larger retention window never restores pruned or never-ingested history.
RPC HISTORY_RETENTION_WINDOW defaults to 120960 ledgers, about 7 days (dated release).
RPC backfills only with BACKFILL=true, from a datastore.
Horizon HISTORY_RETENTION_COUNT defaults to 0 (unlimited); 518400 is the 30-day advice.
Missing Horizon history needs `stellar-horizon db reingest range`.
avoid: Do NOT claim a larger retention window downloads or restores pruned or never-ingested history.
Do NOT use zero for unlimited RPC retention or call 518400 Horizon's default.
golden.notes: Do not require a database size such as 1.3 TB per 30 days or 40 GB per day; it depends on version, filters and workload. Accept a newer dated RPC default.

truth.notes:
GT-54 CORRECTION 2026-07-11: this case owns executable retention, RPC BACKFILL and Horizon reingestion mechanics. The full-history sibling owns component/query boundaries; neither may collapse retention-only behavior into a universal no-backfill claim. GT-54 CORRECTION 2026-07-11: current Horizon source defaults HISTORY_RETENTION_COUNT to 0/unlimited; 518400 is the official one-month recommendation, not the executable default (official pages called it the default until sd-028 was fixed on 2026-07-27). RPC v27.1.1 ships 120960 as a dated binary default, not a hard maximum or universal provider policy. The user's ~1.3 TB/30d figure was not made a required exact claim; exact DB size depends on version, filters, and workload.
Also good if the answer: Mentions changing Horizon ingestion filters also does not retroactively backfill matching historical data; a historical range ingestion is needed. | Caveats storage estimates like 1.3TB/30d as workload/version-dependent rather than a universal constant.
Golden cites: Horizon ingestion storage/retention docs. | RPC retention/data-lake docs. | Horizon filtering docs if discussing retroactive filtering/backfill.
Grade the version-dated executable semantics and product/method boundaries, not an exact database size, provider window, checkpoint floor, or backfill duration. The v25.1 150 GB/<3h/<3 GB figures are release notes, not requirements.
Re-verified 2026-11-02: stellar-rpc v30.0.0 and stellar-horizon v30.0.0 keep these defaults and behaviors. Since sd-028 (2026-07-27) the official Horizon pages state the 0 default, so an answer need not report an official-prose conflict.
Documentation reconciliation 2026-11-09: the official RPC configuring page now explains empty-database startup at the archive tip and why retention alone adds no older ledgers. sd-102 preserves the RPC team's declined request to document the internal-gap corruption sanity check. BACKFILL can create a database from scratch; an empty database counts as gapless. Do not require an otherwise correct answer to recite that sanity check, or treat the owner's omission as a contradiction of the implementation.
